newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: No NZ coalition talks planned, MPs on standby.
newsitem.headline: No NZ coalition talks planned, MPs on standby.

text.p: No coalition negotiation meetings are planned today, a New Zealand First spokesman said on Thursday.
He said work would continue on reports which were being exchanged between the parties.
"There will be work on those reports and when sufficient progress is made then they will meet again," the spokesman said.
Labour Party leader Helen Clark on Wednesday said Labour MPs had been placed on standby should a caucus meeting need to be called at short notice to consider a coalition deal with NZ First.

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the caretaker conservative National government and centre-left Labour over the shape of the new government.
NZ First MPs are confident a final decision can be made before parliament sits next week.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger was expected to announce later on Thursday when parliament would open for the new session.
Parliament must meet by Friday December 13 but under parliament's rules, known as standing orders, it does not sit on Fridays, effectively moving the deadline forward to December 12.
